exchanges.author: c_lisa
exchanges.body: Good MBR. Approved: second Pinnacle class of 9 on 11/16. Can you send me the accuracy root cause today? 99.78 vs 99.8 will come up with the CFO.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Accuracy root cause: 570 mis-picked lines in October; 312 (55%) in aisles 14-15, which we re-slotted 10/12 and which now have look-alike fittings on adjacent faces. Without them we'd have been at 99.90%. Fix, starting today: Omar re-slots the 6 look-alike pairs apart this week, adds part photos to the scanner prompt for those SKUs, and we audit aisles 14-15 daily for two weeks. I expect us back above 99.8% in November.

exchanges.author: c_shawn
exchanges.subject: Re: Marlene Hughes: final warning?
exchanges.body: HR sent Marlene the FMLA paperwork. Can I still give her the points in the meantime? Otherwise others will say it's unfair.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: No points for those absences while HR reviews the FMLA paperwork; if it's approved, they're protected and points would be retaliation. If people ask, it's fair to say leave questions go through HR and that the same rules apply to everyone. Andrea will tell you the outcome.

exchanges.author: c_dale
exchanges.subject: LED retrofit proposal
exchanges.body: Ronan, Brightside Energy quoted $42,000 to replace the 380 metal-halide high bays with LED and motion sensors; they estimate savings of $1,050 a month in electricity, and AEP Ohio's rebate would cover $9,500. Worth doing? Dale

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Worth pursuing: net cost $42,000 - $9,500 rebate = $32,500, savings $1,050 a month, so a ~31-month payback (about 37% a year), plus better light in the aisles where we have mis-picks. It's capital over my authority, so I'll put it in a CER for Lisa with the dock 7 one for January. Dale, can you get the savings estimate backed by our actual kWh from the AEP bills and confirm the rebate is pre-approved?

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Kelly, confirmed: second class of 9 on Monday 11/16, same 6:30 orientation. Thanks!

exchanges.author: c_carrier
exchanges.subject: Re: Dispute: invoice BF-55102
exchanges.body: We've reviewed the gate times. We'll credit 10/27 ($525), but 10/20's driver says he was told at the gate to wait. Revised invoice: $825. Buckeye billing

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Thanks for the 10/27 credit. On 10/20: the clock starts at the appointment only if the truck is on time, and BF-2214 arrived at 10:40 for an 08:00 appointment, so the 2 free hours start at arrival (10:40 to 12:40); it departed 13:15, 0.5 hour after, which our terms round to zero. Our gate staff don't tell late drivers detention applies. Please reissue for $375. Ronan

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: Safety walk 11/5: actions
exchanges.body: Actions from today's walk: (1) Dock 4 lock not engaged: Tina, re-brief all loaders today; Dale, check the lock indicator lights on docks 1-12 by Friday. (2) Aisle 9 overhanging pallets: Shawn, fix today and add a beam check to the 2 p.m. walk. (3) Eyewash tag not signed since 9/12: Beth, inspect and sign today; add to the monthly checklist. (4) Mezzanine handrail loose: Dale, tape off and repair by end of day tomorrow. Good catch on horn use, please tell the drivers.
